nodes.summary: Given a finite list $L$ of blocked channel names, the silent action $\tau$ is always permitted, and an input or an output on a channel $a$ is permitted exactly when $a \notin L$.
nodes.title: Actions permitted by a restriction

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a finite relabelling whose table lists the entries $(a_1, \ell_1), \dots, (a_k, \ell_k)$, where each $a_i$ is a channel name and each $\ell_i$ a visible label. The image of a channel name $a$ under $f$ is $\ell_i$ for the first index $i$ with $a_i = a$, and the input label on $a$ when no entry has name $a$.
nodes.title: Applying a relabelling to a channel name

nodes.summary: Given relations $R$ and $S$ on finite CCS processes, write $P_1 + P_2$ for the nondeterministic choice of $P_1$ and $P_2$. The choice lift of $R$ and $S$ relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when $R(P, Q)$ holds, or $S(P, Q)$ holds, or $P = P_1 + P_2$ and $Q = Q_1 + Q_2$ with $R(P_1, Q_1)$ and $S(P_2, Q_2)$.
nodes.title: Lifting relations through choice

nodes.summary: For CCS processes $P_1$, $P_2$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ with labels over a set of names: if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are strongly bisimilar and $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then the choices $P_1 + Q_1$ and $P_2 + Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar there.
nodes.title: Choice preserves strong bisimilarity in CCS with communication

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system whose states are CCS processes with labels over a set of names, whose labels are CCS labels over those names, and whose transition relation is the CCS transition relation with communication.
nodes.title: Labelled transition system of CCS with communication

nodes.summary: For CCS processes $P$, $Q$, $R$ and a CCS label $a$, the parallel composition $P \mid Q$ has a transition labelled $a$ to $R$ in the CCS transition relation with communication if and only if one of the following holds: $P$ has a transition labelled $a$ to some $P'$ and $R = P' \mid Q$; or $Q$ has a transition labelled $a$ to some $Q'$ and $R = P \mid Q'$; or $a = \tau$ and there are processes $P'$, $Q'$ and…
nodes.title: Transitions of a parallel composition

nodes.summary: For every CCS label $a$ and all CCS processes $P$ and $Q$: if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then so are the prefixed processes $a.P$ and $a.Q$.
nodes.title: Prefix preserves strong bisimilarity in CCS with communication

nodes.summary: The transition relation on CCS processes with labels over a set of names given by the raw step relation for the synchronization function under which an input and an output on the same name, in either order, synchronize to the silent label $\tau$, and no other pair of labels synchronizes.
nodes.title: CCS transition relation with communication

nodes.summary: The complement of the input label on a channel $a$ is the output label on $a$, and the complement of the output label on $a$ is the input label on $a$.
nodes.title: Complement of a visible label

nodes.summary: Two CCS labels are complementary when one is the input on a name $a$ and the other is the output on the same name $a$, in either order. No other pair of labels is complementary; in particular the silent label $\tau$ has no complement.
nodes.title: Complementary labels

nodes.summary: The constant occurrences of a recursive CCS process $P$ are the list of the process constants occurring in $P$, from left to right and with repetitions: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ has none; a constant $A$ has the single occurrence $A$; a prefix $\alpha.Q$, a restriction $Q \setminus L$ and a relabelling $Q[f]$ have the occurrences of $Q$; and a choice $Q + R$ or a parallel composition $Q \mid R$ has the…
nodes.title: Constant occurrences of a process

nodes.summary: Assuming equality of process constants is decidable, the constants of a recursive CCS process $P$ are the list obtained from the constant occurrences of $P$ by removing duplicates, so that every process constant occurring in $P$ appears in it exactly once.
nodes.title: Constants of a process

nodes.summary: Given a relation $E$ on finite CCS processes, its equation closure relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when $P = Q$ or $E(P, Q)$; that is, it is the reflexive closure of $E$.
nodes.title: Reflexive closure of a relation on processes

nodes.summary: A recursive specification $\Delta$, which assigns to each process constant $A$ a body $\Delta(A)$, is guarded when for every constant $A$ the body $\Delta(A)$ is a guarded process.
nodes.title: Guarded recursive specification

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a recursive CCS process, let $\rho$ be a map from its process constants to another set of constants, and let $P\rho$ be the process obtained from $P$ by renaming its constants by $\rho$. Then for each Boolean flag $b$, $P\rho$ is guarded under $b$ if and only if $P$ is guarded under $b$.
nodes.title: Renaming constants preserves guardedness

nodes.summary: Every recursive CCS process $P$ is guarded under the flag $\mathrm{true}$: once an action prefix has been crossed, every constant occurrence counts as guarded.
nodes.title: Every process is guarded beneath a prefix

nodes.summary: For a Boolean flag $b$, recording whether an action prefix has already been crossed, guardedness of a recursive CCS process under $b$ is defined recursively: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ is guarded under $b$; a constant $A$ is guarded under $b$ exactly when $b$ is true; a prefix $\alpha.Q$ is guarded under $b$ when $Q$ is guarded under true; a choice $Q + R$ or a parallel composition $Q \mid R$ is guarded…
nodes.title: Guardedness under a prefix flag

nodes.summary: A recursive CCS process is guarded when all of its constant occurrences lie beneath an action prefix.
nodes.title: Guarded process

nodes.summary: For a set of names, a CCS label is either the silent action $\tau$, the input on a name $a$, or the output on a name $a$.
nodes.title: CCS labels

nodes.summary: Assuming equality of names is decidable, for a recursive specification $\Delta$ the labelled transition system generated by $\Delta$ has the recursive CCS processes as states and the CCS labels as labels, and its transitions $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ are exactly the steps of the structural operational semantics relative to $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Labelled transition system of a recursive specification

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators has the finite CCS processes with restriction and relabelling as states and the CCS labels as labels, and its transitions are the steps of the structural operational semantics of these processes.
nodes.title: Transition system of CCS with restriction and relabelling

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system whose states are the finite CCS processes, whose labels are the actions, and whose transitions $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ are those of the communication-free operational semantics of finite CCS.
nodes.title: Labelled transition system of finite CCS

nodes.summary: Given a map $\rho$ from one set of process constants to another, renaming the constants of a recursive CCS process $P$ by $\rho$ replaces each occurrence of a constant $A$ by $\rho(A)$ and leaves $P$ otherwise unchanged: the inactive process, prefixes, choices, parallel compositions, restrictions and relabellings are kept as they are.
nodes.title: Renaming process constants

nodes.summary: Each finite CCS process over CCS labels is sent to the process with static operators of the same shape: the inactive process goes to the inactive process, the prefix of an action $\alpha$ to a process $P$ goes to the prefix of $\alpha$ to the image of $P$, and a choice or a parallel composition of $P$ and $Q$ goes to the choice or the parallel composition of the images of $P$ and $Q$.
nodes.title: Embedding finite CCS into CCS with static operators

nodes.summary: For all CCS processes $P$ and $Q$ with labels over a set of names, $P \mid Q$ and $Q \mid P$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication.
nodes.title: Parallel composition is commutative up to strong bisimilarity

nodes.summary: For CCS processes $P_1$, $P_2$, $Q_1$, $Q_2$ with labels over a set of names: if $P_1$ and $P_2$ are strongly bisimilar and $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of CCS with communication, then the parallel compositions $P_1 \mid Q_1$ and $P_2 \mid Q_2$ are strongly bisimilar there.
nodes.title: Parallel composition preserves strong bisimilarity

nodes.summary: Given two relations $R$ and $S$ on CCS processes with labels over a set of names, their parallel lift relates a process $U$ to a process $V$ exactly when $R$ relates $U$ to $V$, or $S$ relates $U$ to $V$, or $U = P_1 \mid Q_1$ and $V = P_2 \mid Q_2$ where $R$ relates $P_1$ to $P_2$ and $S$ relates $Q_1$ to $Q_2$.
nodes.title: Parallel lift of two relations

nodes.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For every CCS process $P$ over input, output and silent labels on these names, the parallel composition $0 \mid P$ of the inactive process $0$ with $P$ is strongly bisimilar to $P$ in the communication labelled transition system.
nodes.title: The inactive process is a left unit for parallel composition

nodes.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For every CCS process $P$ over input, output and silent labels on these names, the parallel composition $P \mid 0$ of $P$ with the inactive process $0$ is strongly bisimilar to $P$ in the communication labelled transition system.
nodes.title: The inactive process is a right unit for parallel composition

nodes.summary: For every action $a$ and all finite CCS processes $P$ and $Q$, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS, then the prefixed processes $a.P$ and $a.Q$ are strongly bisimilar there as well.
nodes.title: Prefix preserves strong bisimilarity

nodes.summary: Given a set of names and a set of process constants, the recursive CCS processes are generated by the following constructors: the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$; a process constant $A$; a prefix $\alpha.P$ for a CCS label $\alpha$ and a process $P$; a choice $P + Q$; a parallel composition $P \mid Q$; a restriction $P \setminus L$ for a finite list $L$ of names; and a relabelling $P[f]$ for a CCS relabelling $f$.
nodes.title: Recursive CCS processes

nodes.summary: For a type $A$ of actions, the finite CCS processes over $A$ are built from the inactive process $\mathbf{0}$ by action prefix $a.P$ (an action $a \in A$ followed by a process $P$), nondeterministic choice $P + Q$, and parallel composition $P \mid Q$.
nodes.title: Finite CCS processes

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a partial function that assigns to some pairs of actions $(a, b)$ an action $\sigma(a, b)$. The transition relation $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ on finite CCS processes (built from prefix $a.P$, choice $P + Q$ and parallel composition $P \mid Q$) determined by $\sigma$ is the least relation such that $a.P \xrightarrow{a} P$; if $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ then $P + Q \xrightarrow{a} P'$,…
nodes.title: Operational semantics of finite CCS with a synchronization function

nodes.summary: For every relabelling $f$ and all CCS labels $\alpha$ and $\beta$, if $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complementary, then the actions obtained by relabelling $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with $f$ are complementary.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves complementary actions

nodes.summary: For a relabelling $f$, the silent action $\tau$ is relabelled to $\tau$, an input on a channel $a$ is relabelled to the image of $a$ under $f$, and an output on $a$ is relabelled to the complement of the image of $a$ under $f$, each viewed as a CCS label.
nodes.title: Relabelling an action

nodes.summary: For every relabelling $f$ and all finite CCS processes $P$ and $Q$ with static operators, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators, then the relabellings of $P$ and of $Q$ by $f$ are strongly bisimilar there.
nodes.title: Relabelling preserves strong bisimilarity

nodes.summary: Given a relabelling $f$ and a relation $R$ on finite CCS processes with static operators, the lifted relation is the least relation that relates $P$ to $Q$ and relates the relabelling of $P$ by $f$ to the relabelling of $Q$ by $f$ whenever $R$ relates $P$ to $Q$.
nodes.title: Closure of a relation under one relabelling

nodes.summary: A finite CCS relabelling over channel names is a finite list of entries $(a, \ell)$, each pairing a channel name $a$ with a visible label $\ell$, that is, an input or an output on some channel. The entry $(a, \ell)$ gives $\ell$ as the image of the input on $a$; the image of the output on $a$ is then the complement of $\ell$. The first entry with name $a$ is used, and a name occurring in no entry is mapped to itself.
nodes.title: Relabelling

nodes.summary: For every finite list $L$ of channel names and all static CCS processes $P$ and $Q$, if $P$ and $Q$ are strongly bisimilar in the labelled transition system of finite CCS with static operators, then so are the restricted processes $P \setminus L$ and $Q \setminus L$.
nodes.title: Restriction preserves strong bisimilarity

nodes.summary: Given a finite list $L$ of channel names and a relation $R$ on static CCS processes, the lifted relation relates $P$ to $Q$ exactly when either $R$ relates $P$ to $Q$, or $P = P' \setminus L$ and $Q = Q' \setminus L$ for some processes $P'$ and $Q'$ that $R$ relates.
nodes.title: Lifting a relation through a restriction

nodes.summary: Given a type of channel names and a type of process constants, a recursive specification assigns to each process constant $A$ a defining body: a CCS process expression over those names, which may itself mention process constants (including $A$).
nodes.title: Recursive CCS specification

nodes.summary: Finite CCS processes with the static operators, over a type of channel names, are built from the inactive process $0$ by the prefix $\alpha.P$ of a CCS action $\alpha$ (silent, an input or an output) and a process $P$, the choice $P + Q$, the parallel composition $P \mid Q$, the restriction $P \setminus L$ of $P$ by a finite list $L$ of names, and the relabelling $P[f]$ of $P$ by a finite relabelling $f$.
nodes.title: Static CCS processes

nodes.summary: Let the channel names have decidable equality and let $\Delta$ be a recursive specification, assigning to each process constant $A$ its defining body $\Delta(A)$. The labelled transition relation $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ relative to $\Delta$ on recursive CCS processes, with actions $\alpha$ the CCS labels (silent $\tau$, inputs and outputs), is the least relation closed under the following rules, where…
nodes.title: Transitions of recursive CCS

nodes.summary: The labelled transition relation $P \xrightarrow{\alpha} P'$ on static CCS processes, with actions $\alpha$ the CCS labels (silent $\tau$, inputs and outputs), is the least relation closed under the following rules, where $\alpha.P$ is the prefix, $P + Q$ the choice, $P \mid Q$ the parallel composition, $P \setminus L$ the restriction of $P$ by a finite list $L$ of channel names, and $P[f]$ the relabelling of $P$…
nodes.title: Transitions of static CCS

nodes.summary: The transition relation $P \xrightarrow{a} P'$ on finite CCS processes is the operational semantics of finite CCS whose synchronization function is undefined on every pair of actions. Thus prefix and choice move as usual, and a parallel composition $P \mid Q$ moves only by letting one of $P$ and $Q$ move; there are no communication steps.
nodes.title: Transitions of finite CCS without communication

nodes.summary: Let the names form a type with decidable equality. For labels $a$ and $b$, the synchronization of $a$ with $b$ is the silent action $\tau$ when $a$ is the input on a name $n$ and $b$ is the output on the same name $n$, or when $a$ is the output on $n$ and $b$ is the input on $n$. For every other pair of labels, including any pair involving $\tau$, there is no result.
nodes.title: Synchronization of CCS labels

nodes.summary: The inclusion of visible labels into CCS labels sends the input on a channel $a$ to the input on $a$, and the output on $a$ to the output on $a$.
nodes.title: Visible labels as CCS labels

nodes.summary: A visible CCS label, excluding the silent action.
nodes.title: Visible CCS label

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
